My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for three generations. We always grow winter wheat, then summer maize on the same fields — that is what the soil here is suited for, and what the grain stations will buy. I have about 10 mu of flat irrigated land. My husband does some work in the county seat now, so I manage most of the farming myself, sometimes with help from my son during harvest.

For the wheat, I will plant in October after rotary tilling the maize stubble under. I buy improved seeds from the village cooperative store — the Jimai variety has worked well for us. I apply compound fertilizer as a base before sowing, then add urea at jointing. I irrigate three times: once before winter to help rooting, once at jointing, once at heading. I spray for aphids and powdery mildew when I see them — usually twice a season. I expect around 450 jin per mu if rain cooperates.

For the maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June. No-tillage now — I just direct-seed into the stubble. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, it has been reliable for years. I split fertilizer — some compound at planting, then urea when it is knee-high. I irrigate if August is dry. I spray once for corn borer if I see damage. I expect 550–600 jin per mu.

I will not try new crops this year. Cotton prices are uncertain and I do not know how to grow vegetables commercially. Wheat and maize are what I understand and what buyers will take.
